body:
Implemented in PR #11494.

- Changed: Preserve truncated streamed tool-call arguments as `invalid_tool_call` when the stream ends with `finish_reason: "length"`.
- Tests: Added a deterministic `ChatModelStream` regression test; `git diff --check` passes.
- Validation: Local package checks could not run because this checkout has no installed dependencies.

PR: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchainjs/pull/11494

The reproduction here makes a useful execution-boundary regression: partial parsing can stay available for display, while token-limit termination must never authorize the repaired call's side effect. Complete JSON plus `finish_reason: "length"` is a separate useful negative case.

I maintain [prefix-safe-json](https://github.com/canblmz1/prefix-safe-json). There is now a [standalone installed-package comparison](https://github.com/canblmz1/prefix-safe-json/tree/main/examples/langchain-consumer) using the report's exact `@langchain/openai@1.5.8` and `@langchain/core@1.2.9`. Real `ChatOpenAI.stream()` and PSJ receive the same original mock-SSE fixture. The SDK projects the cutoff as `{message:"hel"}` with no invalid call; caller dispatch through PSJ produces zero effects. Complete JSON plus token-limit termination also produces zero effects. CI checks the candidate tarball in a separate npm consumer.

Would you be interested in trying that boundary in your own development project? This comparison does not provide a production LangChain adapter or exercise AgentExecutor/LangGraph; parsed `AIMessage.tool_calls` cannot recreate raw evidence. An [integration result or blocker](https://github.com/canblmz1/prefix-safe-json/issues/new?template=integration.yml) with your installed versions would help identify whether the boundary is practical. This is an optional comparison, separate from the local fix in #11494.

Two data points in case they help with #11494.

1. On the latest release (`@langchain/core` 1.2.18, `@langchain/openai` 1.6.2, `@langchain/langgraph` 1.5.1), `createReactAgent` with `new ChatOpenAI({ streaming: true })` still runs the cut-off call end to end. A `write_file` call cut in the middle of line 17 of a 40-line file writes the first 16 lines plus part of line 17, the tool returns success, and the agent answers "Done.". Same with `useResponsesApi: true`. With `streaming: false` the call is not run.

2. The same happens when the stream ends with no finish reason at all (the body closes cleanly, no `[DONE]`), which is what a proxy or server dropping the stream looks like. The approach in #11494 keys on `finishReason === "length"` in `ChatModelStream`, so it can't catch that case. Also, in the agent runs above the call is built by `collapseToolCallChunks` (`src/messages/utils.ts`, the `parsePartialJson` call at line 634 on current main), which #11494 doesn't change.

Harness and per-run server logs: https://github.com/simin-yuan/agent-cutoff-bench

Python has the same behaviour; it is tracked in langchain-ai/langchain#41285.
